item.title: Erasmus wants Springboks to turn hurt into heat after opening loss
item.description: South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus wants his team to turn the hurt of their weekend defeat by New Zealand into fuel to get themselves back into contention in the four-test series.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus wants his team to turn the hurt of their weekend defeat by New Zealand into fuel to get themselves back into contention in the four-test series. The Springboks lost their top world ranking when New Zealand [USN:L6N44J052 TEXT:"won the opening test "]33-16 at Ellis Park on Saturday, outscoring their hosts five tries to one as they saw off South Africa’s efforts to muscle them into submission. The world champions had been favourites before the start of the first test of the Kiwis’ eight-match tour. "One could see the hurt on everyone’s faces after Saturday’s match, and we know what we have to do to bounce back strongly this week," Erasmus said as he announced the line-up for the second test in Cape Town on Saturday. "There were a handful of positives and negatives last week, but the main thing that let us down was that we created so many chances, but mistakes at crucial times cost us," Erasmus told reporters on Monday. "We are angry with each other. The coaches did and said stupid things. The players did stupid things on the pitch," added Erasmus. "Me personally, I made wrong calls on some of the tactics we wanted to try and do inside their 22. It didn’t work and that’s on me." Erasmus went back to naming his side early, but kept the All Blacks guessing by putting flanker Siya Kolisi back in the side if the inspirational captain proves his fitness. If not, Paul de Villiers will stay in the starting line-up. "Paul played well on Saturday, and there’s no reason why we should keep him out, but Siya is our captain," the coach said. "Siya has got some strengths, one of them being the attacking breakdown, he’s really good at sorting that out for us, which was the area we struggled with. "There were lots of times that we played badly, not because they did anything illegal, but we couldn’t get the ball away out of the breakdown when we were in really good attacking positions. Siya’s really good at that," Erasmus added.

item.title: Gang attack near Haiti's capital leaves 30 dead
item.description: At least 30 people were killed in a gang attack in the neighborhood of Kenscoff near Haiti's capital of Port-au-Prince, Kenscoff's mayor Jean Massillon told Reuters on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: At least 30 people were killed in a gang attack in the neighborhood of Kenscoff near Haiti's capital of Port-au-Prince, Kenscoff's mayor Jean Massillon told Reuters on Monday. Kenscoff is a hillside town overlooking Port-au-Prince that has been the site of many gang attacks in the last couple of years. Rights groups have reported mass killings, rapes, arson and kidnappings, forcing thousands to flee their homes.

item.title: Hoax article made baseless claim about UK bringing Ceuta migrants to London
item.description: Claims that Britain plans to welcome thousands of migrants from Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta are based on a fake article published on a website impersonating a British newspaper.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Claims that Britain plans to welcome thousands of migrants from Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta are based on a fake article published on a website impersonating a British newspaper. The article, posing as a piece by the Daily Express , falsely claimed that Prime Minister Andy Burnham planned to bring up to 4,000 migrants stranded in Ceuta to Britain, where they would be housed in hotels across London. Social media users widely shared the article , or screenshots of its headline, as authentic, with one post saying "it is over" for Burnham should he follow through with the alleged plan. Reuters found no evidence that the claim was true. The article carried Daily Express branding and closely copied the newspaper's layout and formatting, but it was published on "dailyexpress.uk.com", rather than the genuine Express website, "express.co.uk". A spokesperson for the newspaper's parent company said the report was fake. Britain's interior ministry also told Reuters that Burnham had not proposed transferring thousands of migrants in Ceuta to Britain. Tom Hunt, editorial director at Reach PLC, told Reuters by email: "We have been taking steps to try to remove a cloned website posing as the Express and fraudulently circulating a fake story which was not written or published by us, or the reporter named in the byline." The reporter whose byline appeared on the fake article said in an August 20 post on X that it was not her work and had been published on "a fake Express site". The Express' X account said in response to a screenshot of the article: "This piece was NOT written or published by us." In an email responding to questions about the article, a Home Office spokesperson said: "These claims are simply not true. Any suggestions that we are bringing migrants from Ceuta to the UK are completely bogus. "This government continues to do everything in its power to protect the British public and secure our borders." More than 72,000 people participated [USN:L8N44F14U TEXT:"in a mass border crossing"] from Morocco into Ceuta in late July, although the vast majority returned voluntarily in the following days. Burnham [USN:S8N41Y01A TEXT:"said"] on July 31 that his government had contacted Spain to understand the implications of the crisis and to offer support. VERDICT False. The claim stems from an article published on a website impersonating the Daily Express. A spokesperson for the newspaper's parent company said the Express website had been cloned and that the article was fake. The Home Office also said the claims in the article were false. This article was produced by the Reuters Fact Check team.  Read more  about our fact-checking work.

item.title: Qiagen macht Jonathan Pratt zum neuen Konzernchef

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Qiagen (QIA.DE) holt den Branchenexperten Jonathan Pratt an die Konzernspitze. Der Manager übernehme zum 1. September den Vorstandsvorsitz, teilte der Diagnostikkonzern am Montag mit. Er löst Thierry Bernard ab, dessen Abschied seit Ende vergangenen Jahres feststand. Pratt blickt auf mehr als 25 Jahre Erfahrung in der Branche zurück und führte zuletzt die Filtration Group bis zu deren Verkauf an Parker-Hannifin im August. Zuvor war er in leitenden Positionen unter anderem für die Waters Corporation und die Danaher-Tochter Beckman Coulter tätig. Ungeachtet des Führungswechsels hält Qiagen an seinen Zielen für das laufende Quartal und das Gesamtjahr 2026 fest. Auch die strategische Überprüfung des Geschäfts gehe weiter, erklärte der Konzern. Dabei lotet der Aufsichtsrat mit Hilfe von Beratern aus, wie sich der Wert des Unternehmens für die Aktionäre steigern lässt. Der scheidende Chef Bernard, der seit März 2020 an der Spitze von Qiagen stand, soll den Übergang noch bis zum Jahresende begleiten.

item.title: Reports: 49ers owner Jed York arrested in Ohio over weekend
item.description: San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York was arrested over the weekend in Ohio on two misdemeanor charges, multiple news outlets reported.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York was arrested over the weekend in Ohio on two misdemeanor charges, multiple news outlets reported. York, 46, was arrested on Sunday in East Palestine on counts of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools, WKBN reported. On Monday morning, York pleaded no contest to both charges and was sentenced to one day in the Columbiana County Jail on each count, to be served concurrently with credit for time served, and fined $1,150, according to court records obtained by USA Today and WKBN. York, a native of Youngstown, Ohio, has been CEO of the 49ers since December 2008 and the team's principal owner since 2024. TMZ and the New York Post reported that prosecutors reduced York's original charge of engaging in prostitution to misdemeanor disorderly conduct. --Field Level Media

item.title: Soudan du Sud Deux casques bleus de l'ONU tués dans une embuscade dans l'Etat du Jonglei
item.description: Deux casques bleus de l'ONU ont été tués lundi lors d'une embuscade lors d'une patrouille dans l'État du Jonglei, au Soudan du Sud, a déclaré la mission de l'ONU dans un communiqué.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Deux casques bleus de l'ONU ont été tués lundi lors d'une embuscade lors d'une patrouille dans l'État du Jonglei, au Soudan du Sud, a déclaré la mission de l'ONU dans un communiqué. Sept autres personnes ont été blessées au cours de cette attaque, menée par des hommes armés non identifiés, a précisé la Mission des Nations unies au Soudan du Sud (UNMISS) dans un communiqué. Parmi les blessés figurent trois casques bleus, deux membres du Service national de police du Soudan du Sud et deux membres du personnel civil. L'UNMISS a ajouté avoir déployé une force de réaction rapide afin de sécuriser la zone et d'apporter un soutien aux opérations d'urgence. "De telles violences meurtrières visant le personnel de l'UNMISS, qui œuvre en faveur de la paix au Soudan du Sud, sont inacceptables", a déclaré Anita Kiki Gbeho, chef de l'UNMISS. La mission a appelé à une enquête rapide et a précisé que les attaques contre les casques bleus de l'ONU pouvaient constituer des crimes de guerre au regard du droit international. En début d'année, l'armée du Soudan du Sud avait ordonné à tous les civils et au personnel des missions de l'Onu et d'autres ONG d'[USN:L6N3YR0I6 TEXT:"évacuer"] trois villes de l'Etat du Jonglei avant une opération à venir contre des forces de l'opposition. Le Jonglei, Etat de l'est du pays et frontalier de l'Ethiopie où les Forces de défense du peuple du Soudan du Sud (SSPDF) cherchent à arrêter l'avancée des combattants loyalistes du Mouvement populaire de libération du Soudan en opposition (SPLA-IO), est le théâtre des affrontements les plus violents entre les deux parties.

item.title: Canada to spend C$11 billion to build six new icebreakers, Carney says
item.description: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Monday the federal government would invest more than C$11 billion ($7.95 billion) to build six new icebreakers for the Canadian Coast Guard.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Monday the federal government would invest more than C$11 billion ($7.95 billion) to build six new icebreakers for the Canadian Coast Guard. Speaking in Levis, Quebec, Carney said the ships would be built by Quebec shipbuilder Chantier Davie and would replace the Coast Guard's aging heavy and medium icebreakers. After Russia, Canada has the world's second-largest fleet of icebreakers , which routinely escort U.S. ships heading to the Arctic. Carney has [USN:L1N4000V1 TEXT:"previously pledged "]to ensure Canada has the ability to protect its vast Arctic without relying on any other country. ($1 = 1.3832 Canadian dollars)

item.title: Florida names Georgia Tech transfer Aaron Philo as QB1
item.description: Georgia Tech transfer Aaron Philo will open the season as Florida's starting quarterback, first-year head coach Jon Sumrall announced Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Georgia Tech transfer Aaron Philo will open the season as Florida's starting quarterback, first-year head coach Jon Sumrall announced Monday. The redshirt sophomore won the offseason battle with redshirt freshman Tramell Jones Jr. and will be under center for the Sept. 5 season opener against Florida Atlantic in Gainesville, Fla. Philo followed offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner from Georgia Tech to Florida this offseason and has three years of eligibility remaining. Philo appeared in eight games for the Yellow Jackets across the 2024 and 2025 seasons, completing 57.8% of his passes for 938 yards with two touchdowns and three interceptions. He succeeds DJ Lagway, a two-year starter for Florida who transferred to Baylor following the Gators' 4-8 campaign under former coach Billy Napier and interim coach Billy Gonzales in 2025. Sumrall discussed the QB competition between Philo and Jones earlier this month. "Neither one is just light years ahead of the other," Sumrall told reporters on Aug. 17. "They're both doing really good things. The one thing they both have to continue to work on is who's going to operate the best at the line of scrimmage. We cannot forget motions and shifts, and then protect the football and then just lead. "But they're both doing a great job. They're both supporting each other. They both compete with each other. Do both of them want to start? Yes. But they're doing it the right way in the competition with each other, and they have each other's back." Jones played in two games for the Gators last season, completing 21 of 35 passes for 191 yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions. --Field Level Media

item.title: Japan eyes tax breaks for non-core business sales in governance reform push, sources say
item.description: Japan's government is considering tax breaks on gains from sales of non-core businesses, a move that could accelerate long-delayed corporate restructuring and spur industry consolidation, two people with knowledge of the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Makiko Yamazaki, Miho Uranaka
item.content:encoded: Japan's government is considering tax breaks on gains from sales of non-core businesses, a move that could accelerate long-delayed corporate restructuring and spur industry consolidation, two people with knowledge of the matter said. The plan would remove a major obstacle to companies shedding non-core businesses and redeploying capital into growth areas, in what could become one of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's most significant initiatives to advance corporate governance reform. Under the plan, roughly 30% corporate tax on gains from sales of non-core businesses would be deferred indefinitely, provided companies reinvest the proceeds within several years in acquisitions aligned with their core operations and commit to investing in those businesses, one of the sources said. The proposal is expected to be submitted as part of tax reform requests due at the end of this month, with details to be worked out before a final tax reform package for the next fiscal year is approved at year-end, said one of the sources, who declined to be identified as the matter is still private. POOR CAPITAL ALLOCATION The initiative is modelled on Germany's tax reform in the early 2000s, which largely exempted corporations from taxes on gains from share disposals, helping dismantle the country's dense network of cross-shareholdings and making it easier for companies to reshape their business portfolios. Non-core businesses often remain trapped within sprawling Japanese conglomerates because gains from divestitures are taxed, reducing the incentive to transfer assets to owners better positioned to extract value from them. The result is often inefficient capital allocation. A recent government study found that about 65% of Japanese companies' invested capital remains tied up in businesses that fail to earn their cost of capital, largely offsetting value created by higher-performing units. Such capital trapped in low-return operations is seen as limiting growth investment and weighing on long-term corporate value. Japan has already introduced a range of measures to promote business overhauls over the years, including spin-off tax rules in 2017 and a partial spin-off regime in 2023, but business divestitures taking advantage of those rules have remained relatively limited. A 2020 industry ministry report showed Japanese companies often lack clear divestment criteria and have traditionally prioritised maintaining group size, employment and corporate stability over portfolio reshaping. The tax reform, if implemented, is likely to boost already sizzling M&A activity in Japan. Deal activity involving Japanese companies last year more than doubled from the previous year to a record $353 billion, according to LSEG. Divestitures of Japanese businesses accounted for $44.7 billion of that total.

item.title: Commish: 'We're planning on playing baseball next year'
item.description: With the threat of a potential work stoppage looming, Major League Baseball commissioner Rob Manfred expressed confidence that the 2027 season will proceed.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: With the threat of a potential work stoppage looming, Major League Baseball commissioner Rob Manfred expressed confidence that the 2027 season will proceed. Interviewed Sunday night by ESPN during the Little League Classic, Manfred discussed ongoing negotiations between MLB owners and the MLB Players Association. The current collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1. "We're meeting regularly, which is good," he said. "Every week, we've had days where we've met with the players. It's early, but we've got a lot of work to do, and we're at it. "Look, our goal is to make a deal. We want to make a deal. We want to play baseball next year. We're planning on playing baseball next year." One of the key topics in the labor talks is the owners' goal to establish a salary cap. Owners are seeking a firm salary cap of $245.3 million with a hard floor of $171.2 million. The union remains steadfast against any limit on payroll, instead proposing a "competitive integrity tax" for teams near the bottom in spending which resembles the competitive balance tax for high-spending teams, among several other changes. The Los Angeles Dodgers are cited as a prime reason for a salary cap. The two-time defending World Series champions had a $345 million player payroll last season and paid another $169 million in luxury tax penalties. The Dodgers' tax bill exceeded the Miami Marlins' entire payroll by over $100 million. The Dodgers, New York Yankees, New York Mets and other high-revenue teams, due to their lucrative local TV deals, hold a significant advantage over lower-revenue teams, the owners believe, and MLB feels a salary cap would lessen that edge. Other sticking points between the two sides include service time, the international draft and television revenue. If owners and players can't agree on a new CBA before the December deadline, MLB owners are widely expected to lock out the players until a new deal is reached. --Field Level Media

item.title: ENERGY WATCH: E-Day
item.description: Breaking down what matters today in global energy markets
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Breaking down what matters today in global energy markets By Ron Bousso , ROI Energy Columnist Hello Power Up readers, Welcome to President Donald Trump’s “[USN:S8N40O00O TEXT:"economic D-Day"]” on Iran, Washington’s latest attempt to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the six-month-long conflict in the Middle East. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is scheduled to unveil today at 1 p.m. EDT what he had called "the greatest financial offensive ever marshalled." The U.S. has imposed multiple rounds of punishing sanctions on Tehran over the past five decades, so what more is there to do? It is possible that the Trump administration could roll out new measures that would target Iran's trade partners, in particular [USN:L4N44L0FN TEXT:"China"], which has historically bought most of Iran’s oil. That would be a big gamble in itself, given the tense trade relations between the world’s two largest economies. But here’s another problem for Bessent: the U.S. has already implemented what is likely its most dangerous economic weapon against Tehran: the Navy blockade on Iran’s oil exports. This has sharply restricted its main source of revenue. Iran’s crude oil exports have dropped by nearly 90% in August from their 2025 levels to 259,000 barrels per day, according to Kpler data. Yet Tehran shows little sign of backing down. Iran dismissed the U.S. threat, vowing to shut down all oil exports from the Gulf "if the economic war continues" and issued [USN:L4N44L0G0 TEXT:"a new warning"] that ships cannot pass through the Strait of Hormuz without its permission. In the meantime, the oil market remains under heavy pressure. Oil prices fell slightly early on Monday but are still [USN:L4N44K03U TEXT:"above $90"] a barrel. Traders continue to worry about crude supplies, largely [USN:L4N44L02L TEXT:"dismissing"] claims by the Trump administration that flows through the Strait of Hormuz are far closer to their pre-war level of around 20 million bpd than [USN:L4N44L02L TEXT:"data shows"]. But this focus on crude volumes may actually be the wrong debate. Traders should instead look more at the [USN:L1N44L00N TEXT:"constrained flows"] of refined products around Asia, writes ROI Asia Commodities Columnist Clyde Russell. The global refining system is under enormous pressure, particularly in the United States, which has sharply increased its exports of refined fuels to the global market since the start of the war. U.S. refineries have been operating near maximum capacity for the longest sustained period in over a quarter century, scrambling to capture windfall profits. But history offers a cautionary tale: “Super refining” runs that push plants too hard can cause major failures. More on this [USN:L6N44I0RU TEXT:"here"]. In other news: U.S. LNG producers have shipped [USN:L1N44G12W TEXT:"record volumes"] of the super-chilled fuel so far in 2026, but rising global natural gas prices may soon curb demand from cost-sensitive buyers, ROI Energy Transition Columnist Gavin Maguire wrote. Britain on Monday briefed energy company chiefs on steps to protect their assets after media reports said [USN:L8N44L0FI TEXT:"Iran-linked hackers had shut down a small energy facility"]. As ever, don’t hesitate to contact me at ron.bousso@thomsonreuters.com or follow me on LinkedIn with any questions or thoughts. item.title: Gobierno Trump se dispone a aplicar tasa de más de 100.000 dólares para los visados de trabajo H-1B
item.description: El Gobierno del presidente Donald Trump publicó el lunes una propuesta de reglamento para codificar una tasa sin precedentes de más de 100.000 dólares para los nuevos visados H-1B destinados a trabajadores extranjeros altamente cualificados, que ha sido bloqueada por los tribunales.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Wiessner
item.content:encoded: El Gobierno del presidente Donald Trump publicó el lunes una propuesta de reglamento para codificar una tasa sin precedentes de más de 100.000 dólares para los nuevos visados H-1B destinados a trabajadores extranjeros altamente cualificados, que ha sido bloqueada por los tribunales. La tasa, impuesta por primera vez de forma temporal por Trump el año pasado, eleva drásticamente el costo de los visados, de los que dependen en gran medida los sectores tecnológico, educativo y de investigación. En junio, un juez federal dictaminó que la tasa era ilegal e impidió que la Administración Trump la recaudara. Un tribunal de apelación con sede en Boston está revisando esa decisión, mientras que otro tribunal examina si un juez rechazó correctamente un recurso contra la tasa presentado por un importante grupo empresarial. El aumento temporal de la tasa impuesto por Trump expira en septiembre, un año después de su entrada en vigor. La norma propuesta por el Departamento de Seguridad Nacional de Estados Unidos, publicada el lunes en el Registro Federal, convertiría en permanente una tasa de 103.265 dólares. Podría entrar en vigor a finales de año. El programa H-1B permite a los empleadores estadounidenses contratar a trabajadores extranjeros con formación en campos especializados y ofrece 65.000 visados al año, además de otros 20.000 para trabajadores con títulos de posgrado, con una validez de entre tres y seis años. Antes de la orden de Trump, esos visados solían conllevar tasas de entre 2.000 y 5.000 dólares. La tasa no se aplicaría a los visados concedidos a ciudadanos extranjeros que ya se encuentren en Estados Unidos con visados de estudiante —que constituyen una gran parte de los nuevos beneficiarios de visados H-1B— ni a las renovaciones de visados vigentes. Trump, del Partido Republicano, y otros detractores del programa H-1B afirman que muchas empresas abusan de él para sustituir a los trabajadores estadounidenses por mano de obra extranjera más barata. Sin embargo, las asociaciones empresariales y numerosas empresas han señalado que el programa de visados es necesario para paliar la falta de trabajadores estadounidenses cualificados en determinados puestos y para permitir que las empresas estadounidenses contraten a los mejores talentos. Según documentos judiciales, a finales de febrero, unos 70 empleadores habían abonado la tasa de 100.000 dólares correspondiente a un total de 85 solicitudes de visado.

item.title: Agents: Saints signing All-Pro K Daniel Carlson
item.description: The New Orleans Saints are signing All-Pro kicker Daniel Carlson, his agents confirmed Monday to NFL Network.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The New Orleans Saints are signing All-Pro kicker Daniel Carlson, his agents confirmed Monday to NFL Network. Carlson, 31, has spent the majority of his eight-year NFL career with the Oakland/Las Vegas Raiders. He led the NFL in field goals made (40) and attempted (43) in 2021 and converted a career-long 60-yarder in 2025. The Saints have been holding a competition between kickers Charlie Smyth and Tanner Brown in training camp. Carlson, a fifth-round pick by Minnesota in the 2018 NFL Draft, played two games for the Vikings as a rookie before being released that September and linking up with the Raiders the following month. His career accuracy rate on field goals of 86.9% (225 of 259) in 129 games ranks 10th all-time. The 2022 All-Pro first-team selection has made 95.7% of his extra points (244 of 255). --Field Level Media

item.title: US eyes China overcapacity tariffs of 7.5% before Xi-Trump talks, Bloomberg News reports

item.title: Reports: True freshman Faizon Brandon wins Vols' QB job
item.description: True freshman Faizon Brandon won the battle for Tennessee's starting quarterback job, according to multiple media reports Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: True freshman Faizon Brandon won the battle for Tennessee's starting quarterback job, according to multiple media reports Monday. The five-star recruit from Greensboro, N.C., had been competing with sophomore George MacIntyre. The 6-foot-4, 225-pound Brandon will make his debut for the No. 20 Volunteers in the Sept. 5 season opener against Furman in Knoxville, Tenn. Brandon was ranked the No. 3 quarterback and No. 10 overall player in the Class of 2026 by the 247Sports composite rankings. He passed for over 6,300 yards with 79 touchdowns at Grimsley High School, leading the team to a 35-1 record and two state titles over three seasons as a starter. The 6-foot-6 MacIntyre appeared in two games for the Volunteers last season, completing 7 of 9 passes for 69 yards. He was a consensus four-star recruit in the Class of 2025. --Field Level Media

item.title: Vuelta third stage abandoned after hailstorm in Pyrenees
item.description: A torrential hailstorm in the French Pyrenees forced the abandonment of the third stage of the Vuelta a Espana on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A torrential hailstorm in the French Pyrenees forced the abandonment of the third stage of the Vuelta a Espana on Monday. With 15 km (9.32 miles) remaining of the 174-km ride from Gruissan to Font-Romeu, the skies darkened as the peloton scaled the Col de Mont-Louis and huge hailstones began pelting the riders. Race leader and favourite Tadej Pogacar was seen indicating to the main group to pull off the course and soon afterwards drenched riders were shuffling into a hotel for shelter. Shortly afterwards organisers announced the stage would not resume.

item.title: French potato crop to shrink by 23% after severe weather, growers say
item.description: France's main potato crop is expected to fall 23%, or by about 2 million metric tons, from last year after exceptionally hot and dry weather this summer, growers' group UNPT said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: France's main potato crop is expected to fall 23%, or by about 2 million metric tons, from last year after exceptionally hot and dry weather this summer, growers' group UNPT said on Monday. Potatoes and other summer crops, [USN:L1N44L0DN TEXT:"including maize"], have suffered badly from extreme weather in Europe. The average yield for this year's food potato crop in France is expected to fall 14% from 2025 to 37.4 tons per hectare, the UNPT said in a statement. This would be the second-lowest yield in the past 30 years after 2022, another year marked by severe summer weather. Low yields will compound the impact of a 10% fall in area this year as French growers initially reacted to abundant European supply last year by planting less, UNPT said. The harsh weather also threatens to affect potato size and quality, the UNPT said, calling on processors, including french fry makers, to relax their contract terms. European potato production is concentrated in a northwestern belt that also includes Belgium, Britain, Germany and the Netherlands, all of which have also endured drought and heatwaves. The European Union's [USN:L8N44L0WM TEXT:"crop monitoring service"] on Monday projected that the bloc's potato yield would drop to 34.6 tons per hectare in 2026, 6% below the five-year average.

item.title: Unidade de robótica de montadora chinesa Xpeng é avaliada em mais de US$6,3 bi
item.description: A montadora chinesa de veículos Xpeng anunciou nesta segunda-feira que sua unidade de robótica levantou mais de US$900 milhões em sua primeira rodada de financiamento, estabelecendo um novo recorde para uma única captação privada no setor de inteligência artificial incorporada da China.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A montadora chinesa de veículos Xpeng (9868.HK) anunciou nesta segunda-feira que sua unidade de robótica levantou mais de US$900 milhões em sua primeira rodada de financiamento, estabelecendo um novo recorde para uma única captação privada no setor de inteligência artificial incorporada da China. A rodada de financiamento, liderada pela IDG Capital e apoiada pelos investidores estratégicos Tencent (0700.HK) e Alibaba (9988.HK) , avalia o negócio de robótica em mais de US$6,3 bilhões, afirmou a Xpeng em comunicado. A Gaorong Ventures, uma das primeiras investidoras na empresa de direção autônoma Momenta e na startup de robôs humanóides AgiBot, também participou do financiamento. Os recursos serão utilizados para desenvolver hardware e software de robótica, treinar e aperfeiçoar modelos físicos de IA, coleta de dados, construção de instalações completas para produção em massa e apoiar a expansão global, informou a empresa. A Xpeng tem como meta atingir uma produção mensal de 1.000 unidades de seu robô humanóide IRON até o final do ano, com implantações iniciais em suas lojas de varejo e complexos industriais. As vendas comerciais e entregas na China e nos mercados internacionais estão programadas para começar em 2027. O setor de robótica tem atraído um interesse crescente das montadoras de veículos, que veem semelhanças com o desenvolvimento de veículos inteligentes, incluindo expertise em sensores, software, baterias e gestão da cadeia de suprimentos. Em abril, a TARS Robotics, startup de IA incorporada com sede em Xangai, levantou mais de US$455 milhões em uma rodada de financiamento pré-Série A, um negócio que foi então considerado o maior financiamento privado individual no setor de IA incorporada da China. (Por Qiaoyi Li, Xiuhao Chen, Yukun Zhang e Ryan Woo)

item.title: TV maker TCL mulls spinning off photovoltaic business
item.description: China's consumer electronics maker TCL Electronics said on Monday it is weighing a spinoff and separate listing of its photovoltaic business segment to sharpen focus on its smart home appliances.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China's consumer electronics maker TCL Electronics (1070.HK) said on Monday it is weighing a spinoff and separate listing of its photovoltaic business segment to sharpen focus on its smart home appliances. The spinoff remains at a preliminary deliberation stage and no application has been made to the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, the company said. The photovoltaic segment sells solar power generation equipment and systems, and provides construction, operation and maintenance services. The move comes months after TCL agreed to buy a 51% stake in a joint venture holding Japan's Sony Group's (6758.T) global home entertainment business, including Bravia televisions, in a deal announced in late March . In early July, the company forecast a 40% to 50% rise in half-year profit, mainly underpinned by its TV, display and internet businesses that accounted for three-fourths of the company's revenue in 2025. TCL is due to report its half-year results on Friday.

item.title: Lula et Flavio Bolsonaro au coude à coude à l'approche des élections brésiliennes - sondage Nexus
item.description: L'avance du président brésilien de gauche Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva sur le sénateur de droite Flavio Bolsonaro dans un éventuel second tour des élections présidentielles d'octobre s'est quasiment évanouie, les deux hommes se retrouvant à un point d'écart, selon un sondage Nexus commandé par la banque BTG Pactual, publié lundi.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'avance du président brésilien de gauche Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva sur le sénateur de droite Flavio Bolsonaro dans un éventuel second tour des élections présidentielles d'octobre s'est quasiment évanouie, les deux hommes se retrouvant à un point d'écart, selon un sondage Nexus commandé par la banque BTG Pactual, publié lundi. Selon ce sondage, Lula obtiendrait 46% des voix lors d'un second tour, contre 45% pour Flavio Bolsonaro, fils de l'ancien président Jair Bolsonaro. Dans un sondage réalisé par le même institut le 17 août, Lula recueillait 47% des voix, contre 44% pour Flavio Bolsonaro. Nexus a interrogé 2.006 personnes entre le 21 et le 23 août. La marge d'erreur est de deux points de pourcentage. La droite conservatrice, en général avec le soutien affiché de l'administration Trump, a emporté l'élection présidentielle dans nombre de pays d'Amérique latine ces derniers mois et années : Colombie, Pérou, Argentine, Chili, Équateur, Bolivie et Panama. Cette évolution représente un [USN:L6N42U0F2 TEXT:"renversement spectaculaire"] de la "vague rose" qui avait porté plusieurs gouvernements de gauche au pouvoir au début des années 2020.

item.title: What are Iran's options to escalate further in face of US economic threats?
item.description: U.S. threats to impose "the toughest sanctions in history" to force Iran to buckle to its demands after nearly six months of war have raised the prospect of a new round of escalation in the Gulf.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: U.S. threats to impose "the [USN:L1N44L0FC TEXT:"toughest sanctions"] in history" to force Iran to buckle to its demands after nearly six months of war have raised the prospect of a new round of escalation in the Gulf. How could Iran respond to the economic pressure? CAN IRAN STOP MORE OIL GETTING OUT OF THE MIDDLE EAST? Mohsen Rezaei, the former Revolutionary Guards chief and secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, has already [USN:L6N44K07T TEXT:"threatened to shut down"] oil exports — one of Tehran's main strategic approaches since the war began on February 28. "If the economic war continues, not a single drop of oil will be exported, neither through the Strait of Hormuz nor from anywhere in the Persian Gulf," he said. Iranian attacks and threats to shipping have already stopped most traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, largely shutting down a waterway that carried around a fifth of global energy before the conflict. Although some oil tankers have been moving through the strait in recent weeks, volumes [USN:L1N44L01G TEXT:"remain very low"] and on Sunday Iran blacklisted [USN:L1N44L07X TEXT:"45 tankers"] it says failed to comply with the rules it wants to impose on Hormuz shipping. Missile, drone or speedboat attacks on tankers trying to leave the Gulf have repeatedly pushed up oil prices during the six months of the conflict. Meanwhile, Tehran's Houthi allies have restricted Red Sea shipping with attacks and threats to blockade all [USN:L1N4490KJ TEXT:"Saudi Arabian"] shipping, which carries crude to Asia through the Bab el-Mandeb strait past the group's Yemeni stronghold. While the attacks initially only stopped some vessels, with [USN:L1N4480IA TEXT:"more than half"] still getting through in mid-August, the situation is difficult for shippers with Chinese shipping companies [USN:L4N44A0BL TEXT:"now rerouting"] away from Bab el-Mandeb, according to industry sources. Further attacks, such as the one that targeted a vessel off the main Saudi Red Sea oil terminal [USN:L1N44L08M TEXT:"at Yanbu"] on Monday or a drone strike near the Suez Canal [USN:L6N43W0K4 TEXT:"in early August,"] could raise oil market anxiety levels and crude oil prices. ARE GULF STATES STILL AT RISK OF IRANIAN ATTACK? Iran has threatened to retaliate against any neighbours who take part in U.S. efforts to strangle the country's economy with "earthquake" force. It has targeted Gulf states and Jordan repeatedly during the war, mostly focusing on U.S. bases but also hitting energy infrastructure and other targets. Any intensified attacks that targeted upstream oil or gas facilities could further drive up energy prices in ways that inflict political damage on the Trump administration and could be harder to reverse than attacks on shipping. Targeting power and [USN:L1N40A02Y TEXT:"water desalination"] plants in the hot, parched region would also pose a major risk to U.S.-aligned Gulf monarchies that function as significant financial hubs for the global economy. CAN IRAN ATTACK WESTERN COUNTRIES DIRECTLY? While Western countries are beyond the range of Iran's main munitions, the Revolutionary Guards have historically been willing to find alternative ways of attack. On Monday, Britain said Iran-linked hackers had shut down a [USN:L8N44L0FI TEXT:"small electricity station"] while U.S. officials have said Tehran was likely behind cyber attacks on [USN:L6N43W1HA TEXT:"water plants"] in Minnesota. Iran has not commented on those allegations. Western security services have also accused Iran of recruiting local people to [USN:L1N3TS10T TEXT:"stage attacks or attempt assassinations"] in the West. Iran has denied that.

item.title: Les Houthis revendiquent l'attaque d'un navire au large de l'Arabie saoudite
item.description: Les Houthis yéménites, proches de l'Iran, ont attaqué un navire au large de la ville portuaire saoudienne de Yanbu, en mer Rouge, a déclaré lundi le porte-parole militaire du groupe, Yahya Saree, lors d'un discours télévisé.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Les Houthis yéménites, proches de l'Iran, ont attaqué un navire au large de la ville portuaire saoudienne de Yanbu, en mer Rouge, a déclaré lundi le porte-parole militaire du groupe, Yahya Saree, lors d'un discours télévisé. La compagnie maritime nationale saoudienne Bahri a dit par la suite que l'un de ses navires - l'Amzan - avait été impliqué dans un incident maritime en mer Rouge plus tôt dans la journée, ajoutant que tous les membres d'équipage étaient sains et saufs et qu'aucun blessé n'était à déplorer. La compagnie a précisé qu'elle restait en contact avec le navire et qu'elle coopérait étroitement avec les autorités compétentes. Plus tôt, l'agence britannique des opérations commerciales maritimes (UKMTO) avait rapporté qu'un pétrolier avait été touché par un projectile non identifié à 63 milles marins à l'ouest de Yanbu. L'UKMTO avait ajouté qu'aucun impact environnemental n'avait été signalé. Yanbu est le principal port pétrolier saoudien de la mer Rouge, où sont chargés des millions de barils par jour. Il est devenu la principale voie d'acheminement du pétrole saoudien contournant le détroit d'Ormuz, qui est bloqué par l'Iran. Le trafic maritime au départ de Yanbu est lui-même perturbé depuis que les Houthis ont déclaré, le mois dernier, un blocus contre les navires liés à l'Arabie saoudite en mer Rouge. Les Houthis ont mené des attaques contre des installations pétrolières saoudiennes et des navires en mer Rouge ces dernières semaines, et en juillet, ils ont affirmé avoir pris pour cible les installations du géant pétrolier saoudien Aramco à Yanbu.

item.title: Federal Circuit defines contours of the 'skilled searcher' standard for IPR estoppel
item.description: Jonathan Bowser of Haynes Boone examines a recent decision at the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit that defines the estoppel standard in certain disputes over a patent's validity, providing new guidance on search methodology and hindsight bias.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Bowser
item.content:encoded: Challenging the validity of a patent in an inter partes review (IPR) comes with risk. If the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB) institutes review and issues a final written decision upholding the claims, the IPR petitioner is statutorily estopped from challenging the validity of the patent on any ground that the petitioner "raised or reasonably could have raised during" the IPR. 35 U.S.C. § 315(e). This estoppel extends to validity challenges in district court, the International Trade Commission, or at the Patent Office. For years, the pivotal question has focused on what grounds "reasonably could have [been] raised" when a patent owner seeks to enforce IPR estoppel. The Federal Circuit recently revisited that question for the second time in the same case, this time defining the contours of what grounds could have been "reasonably" raised based on efforts to find the prior art references in the grounds. In Ironburg Inventions Ltd. v. Valve Corp., 64 F.4th 1274 (Fed. Cir. 2023) (Ironburg I), as addressed in my previous article , the Federal Circuit adopted the "skilled searcher" standard for determining whether grounds could have been reasonably raised. Specifically, in Ironburg I, the Federal Circuit held that an IPR petitioner "'reasonably could have raised' any grounds that a skilled searcher conducting a diligent search reasonably could have been expected to discover." In Ironburg Inventions Ltd. v. Valve Corp., 178 F.4th 1328 (Fed. Cir. 2026) ("Ironburg II"), the second time the Federal Circuit addressed this estoppel issue in the same case, the Federal Circuit was asked to define the contours of the "skilled searcher" standard it adopted in Ironburg I. In Ironburg II, the Federal Circuit reversed a grant of estoppel and provided new guidance on search methodology, hindsight bias, and the ground-level nature of the "skilled searcher" inquiry. BACKGROUND In December 2015, Ironburg sued Valve for infringing a patent directed to a video game controller. In April 2016, Valve filed an IPR petition challenging the asserted patent. The PTAB instituted review but upheld the challenged claims in a final written decision in September 2017. In January 2018, a third party, Collective Minds Gaming Co. (CMG), challenged the patent in another IPR after being sued by Ironburg. The PTAB instituted review of CMG's IPR but the CMG IPR was later terminated after settlement between Ironburg and CMG. Valve amended its invalidity contentions in the pending district court case to raise the obviousness grounds presented in CMG's IPR petition. In November 2019, the district court granted Ironburg's motion to estop Valve from raising CMG's grounds. In Ironburg I, the Federal Circuit held that it was error for the district court to grant estoppel simply because CMG had found the prior art references. With no evidence about how diligent CMG's search was, its success in finding the references proved little because CMG could have employed "scorched earth" tactics. Rather, the Federal Circuit held that Ironburg, as the proponent of estoppel, had the burden of proof to show that a skilled searcher conducting a diligent search reasonably could have been expected to discover the prior art references in CMG's grounds. On remand, the district court granted limited discovery as to search efforts to find the references in CMG's IPR grounds that Valve raised in district court. Valve relied on its pre-IPR petition search conducted in 2014, and Ironburg relied on its litigation search conducted in 2023. CMG raised two separate obviousness grounds in its IPR petition, one ground including the "Kotkin" reference and the other ground including the "Koji" and "Raymond" references. Valve's 2014 search did not find Kotkin, Koji, or Raymond, but Ironburg's 2023 search did. The district court granted estoppel, crediting evidence that Valve's searcher searched the exact patent classifications containing Kotkin and Koji and that supplemental keyword-and-citation searches performed by Ironburg's searcher located Raymond. Valve appealed again. The Federal Circuit's analysis centered on the parties' evidence for the Kotkin and Raymond references. AN UNREVIEWABLE NUMBER OF RESULTS The Federal Circuit held that a skilled searcher conducting a diligent search would not have reasonably been expected to discover Kotkin based on the sheer numbers of references. The classification search that Valve's searcher ran returned 26,333 references. The district court had treated the mere fact that Kotkin sat within a searched classification as sufficient. Not so, the Federal Circuit held: "something more is required for estoppel when a classification search alone returns an unreviewable number of search results." This haystack of thousands of references required more. The record itself showed that a searcher would perform keyword and citation searches to narrow the results. Because Ironburg did not offer evidence to bridge the gap between a 26,333-hit search and actual discovery of Kotkin, the evidence could not support estoppel. The Federal Circuit did not expressly require a manual review of search results, but noted that "thousands of sources, not further narrowed in any way, likely cannot be considered discovered for estoppel purposes." TAINTED BY HINDSIGHT For the Raymond reference, the Court found Ironburg's search evidence fatally tainted by hindsight. Ironburg's initial search used forward-and-backward citation searching that pulled in documents post-dating Valve's 2016 IPR petition — including Ironburg's own 2023 design patent, which cites Raymond. Keywords and classifications were then derived from those results, infecting subsequent iterations. The Court found that the searcher's early citation searches seeded the keywords and classifications for every search that followed, so the taint ran through the entire effort. A supplemental search was undertaken, by the searcher's own admission, solely "because there was another reference that had not yet been found." The Court called this "clear evidence of hindsight bias" and held that such evidence "is likely irrelevant to the skilled searcher inquiry" because it sheds light only on what could be found after the relevant petition date. Because the evidence did not show that Raymond could have been reasonably found, it was error to estop on the ground that included Raymond. Notably, the court reversed rather than vacated, directing the district court to consider the validity of Ironburg's patent in light of both grounds. Judge Stark's concurrence adds a useful map. In his view, proving estoppel under the skilled searcher test involves two distinct steps: first, that the prior art reference itself was "findable" by a skilled searcher; and second, that the invalidity ground would have been discovered from the reference(s) found. Judge Stark drew a careful line between "accessible" and "findable" — Kotkin was accessible through a classification search, but not findable amid tens of thousands of results — while a reference cited on the face of the challenged patent is plainly findable. TAKEAWAY For patent litigators, Ironburg II reinforces that IPR estoppel is an affirmative defense that must be proven, not assumed, and it meaningfully raises the evidentiary bar for a patent owner asserting it. Cataloguing the classifications a petitioner searched — or noting that some later searcher eventually located the art — will not carry the day when the search returns an unreviewable collection of references. Patent owners should invest in contemporaneous, well-documented searches that mirror what a diligent searcher would have done at the time of the IPR petition, complete with the narrowing steps that turn a haystack into a finding. Further, patent owners should date-restrict any litigation search to avoid the hindsight trap that sank Ironburg's evidence here. Petitioners, in turn, now have a clearer roadmap for defeating estoppel: attack the size and rigor of the patent owner's search, and probe whether it was quietly reverse-engineered from the references it was meant to find. After two trips to the Federal Circuit, the lesson of Ironburg is a simple one — under § 315(e), locating prior art in a haystack is not the same as finding it. Jonathan Bowser is a regular contributing columnist on patent law for Reuters Legal News and Westlaw Today.

item.title: Images of brides heading for Ceuta in their wedding gowns have been altered
item.description: Two images altered to show women in bridal gowns en route to Ceuta have been shared online as if they are authentic evidence of couples abandoning their wedding ceremonies in Morocco to attempt the crossing to the Spanish enclave in late July.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Two images altered to show women in bridal gowns en route to Ceuta have been shared online as if they are authentic evidence of couples abandoning their wedding ceremonies in Morocco to attempt the crossing to the Spanish enclave in late July. Here are the key details: Both images show women wearing floor-length, white wedding gowns, and one also shows a man in a tuxedo. The first image is an edited screenshot from a video of a group of people running along a highway that connects Morocco to Ceuta. The woman in the unedited video is wearing a white skirt and a pink top. Nina Boudkhili, who identified herself on Instagram as the woman in the video, said in a post that she was not a bride and had been wearing a long skirt that day. Boudkhili also said to Reuters in a private message that she had not been wearing a wedding dress, nor did she see anyone else wearing one. The second image is an edited screenshot of a separate video , showing people running on the shoreline adjacent to the highway in the first video. The unedited video does not show a man in a tuxedo or a woman in a bridal gown. Google’s SynthID detection tool found that the image was likely edited using AI. Verdict: Altered. Both images are digitally altered screenshots from two separate videos. This article was produced by the Reuters Fact Check team.  Read more  about our fact-checking work.

item.title: Ministro de Energía noruego dice que su país perforará en el Ártico sea cual sea la postura de la UE
item.description: El ministro de Energía noruego, Terje Aasland, dijo a Reuters que su país seguirá explotando sus recursos de petróleo y gas en el mar de Barents, independientemente del apoyo de la Unión Europea a una moratoria sobre el suministro de hidrocarburos del Ártico, al tiempo que indicó que ya no se considera la "batería verde" de Europa.
item.dc:creator: Nora Buli, Nerijus Adomaitis
item.content:encoded: El ministro de Energía noruego, Terje Aasland, dijo a Reuters que su país seguirá explotando sus recursos de petróleo y gas en el mar de Barents, independientemente del apoyo de la Unión Europea a una moratoria sobre el suministro de hidrocarburos del Ártico, al tiempo que indicó que ya no se considera la "batería verde" de Europa. Tras la invasión de Ucrania por parte de Rusia en 2022, Noruega se ha convertido en el mayor proveedor de gas natural de Europa, cubriendo cerca del 30% de la demanda de gas tanto de la UE como de Reino Unido. El año pasado, la producción de gas del país se situó cerca de niveles récord, mientras que la producción petrolera tocó su pico desde 2009. Sin embargo, las previsiones oficiales indican que el bombeo descenderá de forma drástica a partir de 2030, a menos que se descubran y exploten nuevos recursos. "En el actual contexto geopolítico y de seguridad, y dada la situación de los recursos, creo que continuar con la actividad en el mar de Barents beneficia tanto a los intereses noruegos como a los europeos", dijo Aasland en una entrevista previa a la ONS, la conferencia bianual sobre energía de Noruega, que se celebra en Stavanger. La UE apoya actualmente la prohibición de nuevas perforaciones en el Ártico por motivos medioambientales, pero está considerando revisar su política en respuesta a las preocupaciones sobre la seguridad energética. Las declaraciones de Aasland ponen de manifiesto que Noruega está haciendo caso omiso de las principales iniciativas de la UE en materia de energías renovables y expansión de la red eléctrica para reducir la dependencia del bloque de los combustibles fósiles, según afirmaron activistas medioambientales. "Los yacimientos descubiertos hoy corren el riesgo de entrar en funcionamiento justo cuando la demanda europea de gas está cayendo drásticamente, lo que plantea un riesgo evidente de activos varados", declaró a Reuters Paal Frisvold, asesor de políticas de Greenpeace. Sin embargo, las empresas energéticas noruegas afirmaron el lunes que seguirán adelante con nuevas perforaciones, con la esperanza de realizar importantes nuevos descubrimientos.

item.title: La India se enfrenta al monzón más débil de las últimas dos décadas, a medida que El Niño gana fuerza
item.description: La India se encamina hacia el monzón más débil de las últimas dos décadas, y se prevé que las precipitaciones al final de la temporada se sitúen en torno a un 15% por debajo de la media a largo plazo, la cifra más baja desde 2009, dijeron dos fuentes de alto nivel del departamento meteorológico.
item.dc:creator: Rajendra Jadhav
item.content:encoded: La India se encamina hacia el monzón más débil de las últimas dos décadas, y se prevé que las precipitaciones al final de la temporada se sitúen en torno a un 15% por debajo de la media a largo plazo, la cifra más baja desde 2009, dijeron dos fuentes de alto nivel del departamento meteorológico. Este monzón débil podría afectar a la producción agrícola, hacer subir los precios de los alimentos y reducir los ingresos rurales en la quinta economía más grande del mundo, donde las lluvias aportan alrededor del 70 % de las precipitaciones anuales del país. La falta de lluvias abundantes en septiembre -mes crucial para la maduración de los cultivos- podría mermar el rendimiento de los cultivos de verano, como el algodón, la soja, el maíz y las legumbres, al tiempo que agotaría la humedad del suelo necesaria para los cultivos de invierno, como el trigo y la colza. "Estamos presenciando el impacto de El Niño en las precipitaciones del monzón. Es probable que sea grave en septiembre, y podríamos registrar un déficit de precipitaciones de dos dígitos", afirmó un alto cargo del Departamento Meteorológico de la India (IMD), que prefirió mantener el anonimato al no estar autorizado a hablar con los medios de comunicación. La India podría registrar unas precipitaciones un 15% por debajo de la media, es decir, el 85% de lo habitual, durante la temporada de junio a septiembre, lo que supondría el nivel más bajo de precipitaciones desde 2009, añadió. Eso supondría casi el doble del déficit del 8% previsto en la previsión inicial del departamento meteorológico. Salvo en algunos estados del este, es probable que la mayor parte del país registre precipitaciones por debajo de la media en septiembre, lo que aumentaría el déficit estacional, añadió. Se espera que el IMD publique su pronóstico oficial para septiembre a finales de este mes. El monzón de este año podría comenzar a retirarse del noroeste del país unos días antes de lo habitual el próximo mes, a menos que se forme un nuevo sistema, según afirmó una segunda fuente del departamento meteorológico, que no quiso revelar su identidad de acuerdo con las normas oficiales. El monzón suele comenzar en junio y empieza a retirarse a partir del 17 de septiembre de las zonas del noroeste del país, para terminar en todo el territorio a mediados de octubre. El Niño se está fortaleciendo y es probable que se intensifique aún más en septiembre, lo que reducirá las precipitaciones en la India, afirmaron. El Niño, un fenómeno climático caracterizado por temperaturas inusualmente cálidas en la superficie del mar en el Pacífico ecuatorial central y oriental, altera los patrones meteorológicos globales y puede provocar condiciones más secas en algunas zonas del sudeste asiático y otras regiones. En el pasado, la India ha registrado precipitaciones por debajo de la media durante la mayoría de los años en los que se ha producido El Niño, lo que en ocasiones ha provocado graves sequías que han destruido las cosechas y han obligado a las autoridades a limitar la exportación de algunos cereales.

item.title: Reports: Browns to open season with Deshaun Watson as QB1
item.description: New Browns head coach Todd Monken opted to stay the course in Cleveland and will start Deshaun Watson at quarterback in Week 1 of the regular season, according to multiple media reports Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New Browns head coach Todd Monken opted to stay the course in Cleveland and will start Deshaun Watson at quarterback in Week 1 of the regular season, according to multiple media reports Monday. The team was informed of the decision Monday, the Cleveland Plain Dealer reported. Watson and Shedeur Sanders competed for the starting job in training camp, rotating reps with the first-team offense in practice and preseason games. Cleveland covets stability at the position, and Watson was viewed as the potential answer when he was acquired from the Houston Texans prior to the 2022 season. As part of the trade, Watson signed a five-year, $230 million contract. But after starting his tenure with the team serving a suspension, he has been hindered by injuries and is just 9-10 as a starter in Cleveland. He hasn't played more than seven games in any of his three seasons with the Browns. Watson did not play last season while recovering from two surgeries to repair his Achilles. Watson tore his right Achilles tendon in October 2024 and a recurrence of the same injury during rehab prompted a second operation. Sanders, a fifth-round pick in 2025, was thrown into the lineup as a rookie. With Watson on injured reserve all season, the Browns began the season with Joe Flacco as the starter but traded him to the Cincinnati Bengals. Dillon Gabriel, a third-round rookie in 2025, was named the starter but Sanders took over in November. He had seven touchdown passes and 10 interceptions in eight games. The Browns begin the 2026 regular season with two road games: Sept. 13 at the Jacksonville Jaguars and the following week at Tampa Bay. Cleveland's first home game is Sept. 27 against the Carolina Panthers. Watson likely needs a strong start to the regular season to win back a fan base that appears to be running out of patience. Watson was showered with boos by home fans during Saturday's preseason game and said it was "personal." He played the second half against Buffalo and completed 5 of 12 passes for 36 yards and an interception "It's a little bit (more) personal than that. So I think it's a disrespectful thing," Watson said of being booed at home. "So yeah, I mean, I'm going to keep whatever I feel with me and my family internally on how I feel about that. And yeah, just move on." Watson turns 31 the day after the Week 1 opener. Monken, hired to replace Kevin Stefanski, is a first-time head coach after serving as the Baltimore Ravens' offensive coordinator for the last three seasons. He said Watson and the Browns can avoid being booed at home by playing better, but also offered his perspective on Watson's response. "I see the competitor in him. I see the every-day work he puts in, and he wants to be back," Monken said. "He wants to get back to where he was as best he can, and that's hard. And again, I think the moment just got him after the game, and it can get all of us." --Field Level Media
